# Read-set byte controls from .174

`golden-2.etf` and `golden-32.etf` were generated by the real published .174
plan/session/transaction implementations from commit
`13a59668509989dd2ae01c1b71668ef6edc0f05c` on OTP 28.0.2. They contain synthetic
test material, a public test identity, signed plan/envelope bytes, the signed
canonical body, signature and semantic ID. No fleet ledger contents or node
private keys are included. The fixture generator uses an explicitly public,
deterministic test seed, not an operational identity.

The producer loaded every predicate as an atom. Both fixtures have ascending
UTF-8 predicate-name/arity order, including the small-map boundary at 32 keys.
The new codec must reproduce the *whole* signed artifacts and semantic IDs,
not merely decode them successfully. Consumer tests keep the predicate names
opaque and must not allocate those atoms.

Baseline source SHA-256:

- `quod_transaction.erl`: `760c0487882922c2b66ba60fc8d081f5355fa6eb6823c344b012ef262f83faf1`
- `quod_dtx.erl`: `646e8dc13c137f49edcc8ceceb3d7d5bb024e73424ffc7220462d973baa03064`
- `quod_proof_session.erl`: `abc1e00a91528072b534d4e6ccfb045d53e53cf8f198a178e1d980dd9f0c7656`

Fixture SHA-256:

- `golden-2.etf`: `1ad978eee25f17454b7ad6c552ccb43df8103a6c39e61ec4430c3f604eaf5e61`
- `golden-32.etf`: `895090f7161a044c1d755bf2903304627625036ce043a1b661d33419580df641`

The read-only retained-fleet scan is separate evidence, not inferred from
these examples. Its source, carrier-positive controls, per-file hashes,
namespace counts and failed scan attempts are in the S8 read-set handoff.
No compatibility claim is made for historical hash-ordered read-sets above
32 keys; the scan found none in the retained population.
